blocks.title: Rules Of Thumb
blocks.text: Static for hot paths and small type sets. Watch for bloat when one generic is instantiated with dozens of types. Compile-time resolution is what lets associated types, `Self` returns, and generic methods work here — and not under `dyn`.

blocks.title: The Motivating Case
blocks.text: A `Vec<T>` with generic `T` holds exactly one type. `Vec<Box<dyn Draw>>` holds buttons, checkboxes and text fields together.

`dyn Any` + `downcast_ref::<Button>()` gives `Option<&Button>`.

blocks.q: When is object safety actually checked?
a_bullets: When you write `dyn Trait`, not when you define the trait.
A dyn-hostile trait is perfectly fine if only used generically.
So `Clone` and `PartialEq` are not broken — just not erasable.

blocks.title: Design For Both
blocks.text: Want a trait usable generically and as `dyn`? Keep methods `&self`-receiving, non-generic, and `Self`-free in their signatures.

items: `Vec<Box<dyn T>>` also pays one extra indirection per element.
Static binary grows with (types x generic functions).
Dynamic emits one vtable per type and one function body.
Static supports generic methods, `Self` returns, free associated types.
`dyn` forces associated types to be spelled: `dyn Iterator<Item = u32>`.
Static erases nothing, so misuse fails in full detail up front.

blocks.title: API Stability
blocks.text: Adding a generic parameter is a breaking change to every caller signature. `dyn` keeps signatures fixed and localizes the churn inside your crate.

blocks.text: `dyn` overhead is usually invisible next to an allocation, an I/O wait, or a cache miss. Reach for it freely outside measured hot paths.

caption.text: Rust's trait system is one idea — a contract — wired into four different machines: generic bounds, monomorphization, vtables, and coherence. This handbook walks all of them, from `impl Trait for Type` through the orphan rule, object safety, associated types, and the blanket impls that quietly close your API forever. If you have ever stared at E0038, E0117 or E0119 and guessed at the fix, slide 10 is your lookup table.
